audience: Israel — and anyone hearing creation’s beginning
setting: God is creating the heavens and the earth from nothing — speaking light, order, and life into being.

audience: Israel — and anyone hearing that people are made in God’s image
setting: On the sixth day God makes man in His own image, male and female, and blesses them to be fruitful.

audience: Israel learning the seventh day
setting: The heavens and the earth are finished; God rests on the seventh day and blesses it.

about: The serpent, Eve, Adam, and the Lord God
audience: Adam and Eve in the garden — and all of us after the fall
setting: In Eden, the serpent tempts Eve and Adam; sin enters the world and fellowship with God is broken.

about: The Lord, speaking through Moses’ account of Noah
audience: Noah’s household — and every generation under God’s promise
setting: The world is filled with violence; God saves Noah’s family through the flood and makes a covenant.

audience: Abram
setting: God calls Abram to leave home for a land He will show him; promise and blessing for the nations begin.

audience: Abraham (and Isaac beside him)
setting: God tests Abraham; Isaac is nearly offered on Moriah, then God provides a ram.

audience: Moses at the burning bush
setting: At the burning bush, the Lord calls Moses to free Israel from Egypt.

audience: Israel at the Red Sea
setting: Israel is trapped at the sea; God parts the waters and overthrows Egypt’s army.

audience: Israel at Sinai
setting: At Sinai, God speaks the Ten Commandments to Israel as covenant law.

audience: Joshua
setting: The Lord said this to Joshua: Charge to Joshua.

audience: Israel remembering kindness and redemption
setting: The narrator of Ruth said this to Israel remembering kindness and redemption: Ruth and Boaz.

audience: Samuel in the Lord’s house
setting: The Lord (and young Samuel) said this to Samuel in the Lord’s house: Samuel hears God.

audience: Israel facing Goliath — and anyone facing a giant fear
setting: David (and the narrator) said this to Israel facing Goliath — and anyone facing a giant fear: David and Goliath.

audience: David
setting: Nathan the prophet (from the Lord) said this to David: Davidic covenant.

about: The narrator of Job (and the Lord in heaven’s counsel)
audience: Readers watching Job’s trial begin
setting: The narrator of Job (and the Lord in heaven’s counsel) said this to Readers watching Job’s trial begin: Job’s testing begins.

audience: Job
setting: The Lord said this to Job: God answers Job.

audience: Anyone who needs a Shepherd
setting: David sings of the Lord as his shepherd who leads, restores, protects through the valley, and prepares a table — goodness and mercy all his days.

audience: God — and any heart needing mercy after failure
setting: After Nathan confronts David about Bathsheba, David pleads for mercy, a clean heart, and restored joy.

about: Israel’s refuge hymn — sung for those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High
audience: Those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High
setting: A hymn of refuge under the shadow of the Almighty — protection for those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High.

about: A worshiper in love with God’s Word — walking by law, precepts, and path
audience: Anyone learning to walk by Scripture
setting: The great acrostic love-song to God’s Word — law, precepts, and path for the pilgrim who walks by Scripture.

audience: A son (and every reader seeking guidance)
setting: Solomon giving wisdom said this to A son (and every reader seeking guidance): Trust in the Lord.

audience: Weary Judah — and anyone waiting on the Lord
setting: Comfort ye my people: the Lord comes as a shepherd who gathers the lambs, and they that wait on Him renew their strength.

audience: Israel — and all who look to the Suffering Servant
setting: The Servant suffers for sins; He is wounded for our transgressions.

audience: The exiles in Babylon
setting: Jeremiah writes to the first exiles in Babylon: seek the peace of the city; God’s thoughts toward them are peace, and an expected end.

audience: Readers watching faith in the fire
setting: Three friends refuse to bow to the image and are thrown into the fiery furnace.

audience: Readers watching prayer under pressure
setting: The narrator of Daniel said this to Readers watching prayer under pressure: Daniel in the lions’ den.

about: The narrator of Jonah (and the Lord speaking)
audience: Jonah — and anyone running from mercy
setting: The narrator of Jonah (and the Lord speaking) said this to Jonah — and anyone running from mercy: Jonah and Nineveh.

audience: His disciples on the mount (and you today)
setting: Jesus teaches the Sermon on the Mount: heart righteousness, prayer, and the narrow way.

audience: His disciples who worry about tomorrow
setting: Jesus said this to His disciples who worry about tomorrow: Do not be anxious.

audience: The weary and heavy laden
setting: Jesus said this to the weary and heavy laden: Come unto Me.

audience: The disciples in the boat
setting: Jesus (and Matthew’s account) said this to the disciples in the boat: Walking on the water.

audience: The disciples — and all nations
setting: The tomb is empty; Jesus meets the women and the eleven, and sends them to teach all nations.

audience: Readers hearing why John is dead — and disciples who come to bury him
setting: Herod has John the Baptist beheaded; John’s disciples bury him and go tell Jesus.

audience: The hungry crowd — and the disciples who thought five loaves were not enough
setting: Jesus withdraws, then feeds about five thousand men with five loaves and two fishes.

audience: His own country that stumbled at Him
setting: Jesus is rejected at Nazareth: a prophet is not without honour, but in his own country.

audience: Readers hearing why John is dead
setting: Herod has John the Baptist beheaded after the daughter of Herodias asks for his head.

audience: The hungry multitude — and the apostles just returned
setting: Jesus feeds about five thousand with five loaves and two fishes in a desert place.

audience: The disciples in the boat, toiling in rowing
setting: Jesus walks on the sea to the disciples, and they are sore amazed.

audience: His fearful disciples in the storm
setting: Jesus said this to His fearful disciples in the storm: Peace, be still.

audience: The disciples — and the little children brought to Him
setting: Parents bring little children to Jesus; the disciples rebuke them; Jesus is much displeased and welcomes the children into His arms.

audience: His disciples learning faith and prayer
setting: Jesus said this to His disciples learning faith and prayer: Faith and prayer.

audience: Mary
setting: Gabriel (and ultimately God) said this to Mary: Annunciation.

audience: Shepherds — and all who hear of Jesus’ birth
setting: Luke (and the angels’ word) said this to Shepherds — and all who hear of Jesus’ birth: Nativity.

audience: The seventy being sent
setting: Jesus sends seventy others; they return with joy that even the spirits are subject through His name.

audience: A lawyer testing Him — and every neighbor-watcher
setting: A lawyer asks who is my neighbor; Jesus tells the parable of the Good Samaritan.

audience: Martha and Mary
setting: Martha is cumbered with serving; Mary sits at Jesus’ feet, and He says one thing is needful.

audience: Zacchaeus — and all who murmur that He is gone to be guest with a sinner
setting: In Jericho Jesus calls Zacchaeus down from the sycamore: the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

audience: Jerusalem as the King draws near
setting: Jesus rides toward Jerusalem; the multitude praises God, and He weeps over the city, then cleanses the temple.

audience: Sinners drawing near — and Pharisees listening
setting: Jesus said this to Sinners drawing near — and Pharisees listening: Lost sheep, coin, and son.

audience: His disciples in Gethsemane
setting: Jesus said this to His disciples in Gethsemane: Gethsemane.

audience: Readers meeting the Word made flesh
setting: John the apostle said this to Readers meeting the Word made flesh: Prologue.

audience: Nicodemus (and every seeker of new birth)
setting: At night in Jerusalem, Jesus teaches Nicodemus that new birth by the Spirit and faith in the lifted-up Son bring eternal life.

audience: The woman at the well — and her town
setting: Jesus said this to the woman at the well — and her town: Living water.

audience: His hearers — sheep who know His voice
setting: Jesus is the Good Shepherd who gives His life for the sheep; His own know His voice.

audience: Martha, Mary, and those at Lazarus’ tomb
setting: Jesus said this to Martha, Mary, and those at Lazarus’ tomb: Lazarus raised.

audience: His disciples the night before the cross
setting: Jesus said this to His disciples the night before the cross: Upper room comfort.

audience: His disciples abiding in Him
setting: Upper room: footwashing, comfort, true vine, and high priestly prayer the night before the cross.

audience: Readers standing near Jesus’ death
setting: John (witness of the cross) said this to Readers standing near Jesus’ death: Arrest, trials, crucifixion; “It is finished.”.

audience: Mary, the disciples, and Thomas — and you who believe
setting: The risen Jesus (through John) said this to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas — and you who believe: Resurrection appearances.

audience: Theophilus — and the waiting church
setting: Luke said this to Theophilus — and the waiting church: Ascension.

audience: Jerusalem at Pentecost
setting: Jesus ascends; the Spirit falls at Pentecost; the church is born in Jerusalem.

audience: Saul of Tarsus
setting: The risen Jesus (and Luke’s account) said this to Saul of Tarsus: Paul’s conversion.

audience: Readers watching faith in prison
setting: Luke (with Paul and Silas) said this to Readers watching faith in prison: Philippi jail.

audience: Believers in Rome (and you today)
setting: Paul said this to Believers in Rome (and you today): Letter to Rome.

audience: Believers learning life in the Spirit
setting: Paul teaches believers in Rome about life in the Spirit: no condemnation, adoption, and God working all things for good for those who love Him.

audience: The church at Corinth learning real love
setting: Paul said this to the church at Corinth learning real love: Love chapter.

audience: Believers holding the resurrection
setting: The resurrection of Christ and of the dead; final instructions and greetings.

audience: The church at Corinth in affliction
setting: Paul said this to the church at Corinth in affliction: God of all comfort.

audience: Believers learning strength in weakness
setting: Paul said this to Believers learning strength in weakness: Thorn and grace.

audience: The churches of Galatia
setting: Paul said this to the churches of Galatia: Freedom in Christ.

audience: Believers putting on God’s armor
setting: Finally, be strong in the Lord: put on the whole armor of God against the wiles of the devil.

audience: the church at Philippi (and you today)
setting: Paul said this to the church at Philippi (and you today): Letter from prison.

audience: Believers learning prayer instead of worry
setting: Paul writes from prison to Philippi: rejoice, do not be anxious, the peace of God guards hearts; contentment in every state through Christ.

audience: Believers setting their minds above
setting: Paul said this to Believers setting their minds above: Life hidden with Christ.

audience: Believers grieving with hope
setting: Paul said this to Believers grieving with hope: Comfort in Christ’s coming.

audience: Timothy (and every timid heart)
setting: Paul said this to Timothy (and every timid heart): Spirit of power and love.

audience: Hebrew believers holding faith
setting: The hall of faith: elders who believed God when they could not yet see the promise.

audience: Believers running with patience
setting: Run with patience the race set before you, looking unto Jesus; the Father chastens sons He loves.

audience: Scattered believers under trial
setting: James said this to Scattered believers under trial: Faith under pressure.

audience: Believers casting care on God
setting: Peter said this to Believers casting care on God: Humble under God’s hand.

audience: Beloved children learning to test the spirits
setting: John tells beloved children to test the spirits: not every spirit is of God, but greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.

audience: Beloved children learning God’s love
setting: John urges the church to love one another because love is of God: whoever loves is born of God and knows God, and God is love.

audience: The seven churches — and every reader
setting: John (from Jesus Christ) said this to the seven churches — and every reader: Revelation opening.

audience: The church hoping for the new creation
setting: Christ returns; new heaven and new earth; the river of life; “Even so, come, Lord Jesus.”.

audience: Anyone in trouble who needs a refuge
setting: When the earth shakes and nations rage, this psalm declares God is a present refuge and strength — “be still, and know that I am God.”

about: A Sabbath song in Israel’s worship — thanksgiving that God’s works still make the heart glad
audience: Worshipers giving thanks for God’s works
setting: A Sabbath song of thanksgiving in Israel’s worship: the psalmist praises the Lord because His works make the heart glad, the wicked will not last, and the righteous still flourish in old age.

about: Israel’s congregation — calling all lands to enter His gates with thanksgiving
audience: All lands called to joyful worship
setting: A call for all lands to enter the Lord’s gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise.

audience: Anyone fighting fear with faith
setting: David faces fear of enemies and waits on the Lord as his light and salvation.

audience: Anyone tasting that the Lord is good — and the brokenhearted
setting: David, after escaping Abimelech, teaches: the Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves those of a contrite spirit.

audience: Anyone who needs to know they are fully known by God
setting: David marvels that God searches him, knows him fully, formed him in the womb, and leads him in the everlasting way.

audience: Anyone whose soul is downcast
setting: Sons of Korah: a downcast soul thirsts for God and talks itself back toward hope.

audience: Travelers and anyone needing help from the Lord
setting: A song of ascents for travelers: help comes from the Lord who made heaven and earth and never sleeps.

audience: the church at Philippi (and you today)
setting: Paul writes from prison to Philippi: rejoice, do not be anxious, the peace of God guards hearts; contentment in every state through Christ.

audience: the church at Corinth facing temptation (and you today)
setting: Paul warns Corinth from Israel’s wilderness failures and promises God is faithful in temptation.

audience: His disciples — and all who guard the vulnerable
setting: In Capernaum Jesus teaches humility with a child in their midst and warns against despising little ones whose angels behold the Father’s face.

audience: Peter and the disciples learning how far forgiveness goes
setting: Peter asks how often to forgive; Jesus answers seventy times seven and tells the parable of the unforgiving servant.

audience: Believers learning kindness after the old life
setting: Paul urges the church to put off bitterness and be kind and forgiving to one another, as God in Christ forgave them.

audience: Believers putting on love as God’s chosen ones
setting: Paul tells the Colossians to put on mercy and forbear one another, forgiving as Christ forgave them.

audience: Israel, Abraham’s seed whom He chose from the ends of the earth
setting: The Lord names Israel His servant, the seed of Abraham His friend, taken from the ends of the earth.

audience: Israel in exile whom He told Fear thou not — and you when you need to hear I am with thee
setting: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

audience: Israel watching those incensed against them come to nothing
setting: They that were incensed against Israel shall be ashamed; they that strive with them shall perish and become as nothing.

audience: The one whose right hand the Lord holds — Israel then, and you when you cannot hold yourself up
setting: For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

audience: Jacob called a worm — and you when you feel small in the threshing
setting: Fear not, thou worm Jacob: the Lord will help, and Israel shall thresh the mountains.

audience: The poor and needy who seek water and find none — and you when your tongue fails for thirst
setting: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the LORD will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them.

audience: Believers casting care on God under pressure
setting: Peter closes his letter: humble yourselves under God’s hand, cast all your care on Him, for He cares for you, and resist the devil.

audience: Anyone learning a straight path for work and plans
setting: Solomon’s proverbs on plans and work: commit your works to the Lord so your thoughts rest on Him, not only on your own scheming.

audience: Fathers, children, and households in the church
setting: Paul turns to the household: children obey, fathers do not provoke their children to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

audience: Believers in spiritual battle (and you today)
setting: Finally, be strong in the Lord: put on the whole armor of God against the wiles of the devil.

audience: Wives, husbands, children, and fathers in Christ
setting: Paul addresses the household: fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.

audience: Disciples who were keeping children away, and the children themselves
setting: Parents bring little children to Jesus; the disciples rebuke them; Jesus says, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me.

audience: Weary Judah — and anyone waiting on the Lord
setting: Comfort ye my people: the Lord comes as a shepherd who feeds His flock, gathers the lambs, and gently leads those that are with young.

audience: Exiles who need to know they belong to God
setting: The Lord names and redeems His people: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee; I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.

audience: Anyone afraid in enemy territory
setting: When the Philistines took David in Gath, he says: what time I am afraid, I will trust in Thee — God bottles every tear.

audience: His own soul — and you when all that is within you has not yet blessed His name
setting: David opens this psalm by commanding his own soul: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name.

audience: His own soul — and you when His benefits are easy to forget
setting: Still speaking to his soul, David says: forget not all His benefits.

audience: The soul that needs forgiveness, healing, and renewal
setting: David names why the soul should bless the Lord: He forgives iniquity, heals diseases, redeems from destruction, and satisfies with good things.

audience: Them that fear Him — and you when you need mercy that actually removes the sin
setting: David measures the Lord’s mercy: merciful and gracious, slow to anger; as far as the east is from the west He has removed our transgressions.

audience: Them that fear Him — and you when you need a Father who knows you are dust
setting: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear Him; He knows our frame.

audience: All His works in all places of His dominion
setting: The Lord has prepared His throne in the heavens; David calls angels and all His works to bless the Lord.

audience: Hebrew believers holding fast to Christ
setting: Be content with such things as ye have: He hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

audience: Timothy (and every timid heart)
setting: Paul, from prison, tells Timothy to fan the gift of God: God has not given a spirit of fear, but of power, of love, and of a sound mind.
